And one of the bystanders said
that one hundred and fifty-eight dinars was the handful that was given to him.
And it is also said
that when Saladin was encamped against Acre,
and was riding out on a certain day with the Qadi of the army by his side,
a certain Jewish man cried out and said,
"I appeal to the law of the Muslims!"
And the servants asked him,
"Who is your adversary? And who has wronged you?" And the Jew replied,
"The Sultan is my adversary,
and his servants have wronged me."
And when Saladin heard this, he did not become angry,
but quickly dismounted from his horse,
and the Qadi dismounted as well.
And they brought the Jew,
and Saladin made him stand beside him.
And the Jew said,
"I am a Jewish man, a merchant from Damascus,
and I was coming by sea from Alexandria
with twenty loads of sugar with me.
And when [the ship] drew near to the harbor of Acre,
your servants plundered me,
and they said to me,
'You are an infidel,
and your property belongs by right to the Sultan.'"
And Saladin gave orders, and those who had taken the sugar were brought.
And when they confessed that they had deposited it in the treasury,
he ordered the treasurers,
and they paid the Jew the value of the sugar.
And on another day, when he was sitting,
and with him were the nobles,
the young page-boys began to play with each other.
And when one of them threw a shoe at his companion,
the shoe fell beside the knee of Saladin.
He, however, turned his face to the other side,
and began to converse with the one who was sitting near him,
and feigned as if he had not seen the deed.
And on another day he became thirsty,
and asked for water.
And the servants said to one another,
"Bring water!"
Yet they were negligent and did not bring it.
And again he asked, up to five times.
And when they brought it,
he took and drank without becoming angry at all.
And on another day, when he had risen from an illness and entered the bathhouse,
he asked for cold water.
And when they brought it,
a little of the water splashed onto his body.
And when he shuddered,
because he was weakened,
he did not wish to drink.
And he waited an hour and his thirst grew intense,
and he was in distress and asked for water.
And when the one who was serving him drew near to him,
from his fear his hands trembled,
and the cup fell,
and all that cold water was poured out onto his body.
